description: Exact Nesquena frontend assertions superseded by intentional Hermes UI contracts. Backend, API, runtime, packaging, and all non-listed upstream tests remain mandatory.

replacements.reason: Hermes UI keeps the upstream Help pane and documentation link but retargets issue reporting to the downstream HermesUI repository.
Hermes UI keeps the composer authoritative while typing and exposes Settings through its accessible modal and shortcut outside editable controls.
Hermes UI's expanded mobile customization moves the equivalent containment rule beyond the upstream test's fixed 5,000-character source window.
Hermes UI preserves Ctrl/Cmd+K while additionally synchronizing its mobile session tabs; the upstream assertion requires the old exact statement sequence.
Hermes UI replaces the upstream edge-guard drawer gesture with session-first mobile navigation.
Hermes UI uses a session-first phone surface and hamburger-only navigation instead of the upstream full-screen panel rail.
Hermes UI assigns horizontal swipe to adjacent sessions rather than the upstream PWA panel drawer.
Hermes UI creates a new Untitled session from its session-first mobile surface rather than the upstream titlebar control.
Hermes UI intentionally removes the upstream mobile titlebar new-chat control.
Hermes UI's phone titlebar is intentionally minimal and does not expose the upstream reload control.
Hermes UI replaces the upstream mobile sidebar header composition.
Hermes UI intentionally brands its installable frontend as HermesUI.
Hermes UI intentionally brands its installable frontend as HermesUI while preserving valid manifest JSON.
Hermes UI intentionally brands its root manifest as HermesUI.
Hermes UI replaces edge-drawer swiping with adjacent-session swiping.
Hermes UI replaces the upstream edge-drawer gesture contract.
Hermes UI removes the upstream edge guard and validates interactive-target exclusions on its adjacent-session gesture.
Hermes UI's horizontal gesture navigates sessions rather than opening the drawer.
Hermes UI adds accepted-steer projection into the active session dashboard while preserving owner scoping.
Hermes UI moves Select from an appended text row to the persistent session header.
Hermes UI builds share URLs relative to the application mount instead of the upstream root-relative contract.
Hermes UI uses mount-relative public-share assets instead of upstream root-relative /static paths.
Hermes UI keeps share actions but constructs the resulting URL from the mounted application root.
Hermes UI keeps session search collapsed until requested and uses its own accessible header control composition.
Hermes UI hides redundant folder filters until at least one real folder exists.
